candidates.exact_span: The permittee may apply for a testing frequency reduction upon the successful completion of the first four consecutive quarters of testing for a test species, with no lethal or sub-lethal effects demonstrated at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether FY2025 monitoring was required quarterly versus at a reduced frequency depends on whether these eligibility conditions (four consecutive quarters, no lethal/sub-lethal effects at or below critical dilution) are met; different readings also affect whether missing quarterly results reflect a documented no-data state versus an unresolved obligation (C).

candidates.exact_span: If granted, the monitoring frequency for that test species may be reduced to not less than once per year for the less sensitive species (usually the vertebrate species) and not less than twice per year for the more sensitive test species (usually the invertebrate species).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The applicable monitoring schedule for each WET test species in FY2025 turns on whether a reduction was granted and how 'less sensitive' versus 'more sensitive' species are identified; misclassification changes required test counts and whether apparent gaps are missing evidence or compliant reduced-frequency monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must certify in writing that no test failures have occurred and that all tests meet all test acceptability criteria above.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A granted frequency reduction is conditioned on written certification; whether that certification exists and what it attests affects whether reduced monitoring was actually applicable in FY2025 and how to classify periods without ordinary reported results.

candidates.exact_span: In addition, the permittee must provide a list with each test performed including test initiation date, species, and NOECs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This list is part of the evidence package for a frequency reduction; its presence, completeness, or interpretation affects whether missing-data cases can be classified as documented conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence of required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Upon review and acceptance of this information, the agency will issue a letter of confirmation of the monitoring frequency reduction.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a frequency reduction was in effect during FY2025 depends on agency acceptance and issuance of the confirmation letter; without it, monitoring obligations may remain at the default frequency and missing-result semantics differ.

candidates.exact_span: If any test demonstrates lethal or sub-lethal effects at or below the critical dilution at any time during the life of this permit, three monthly retests are required.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether a test showed lethal or sub-lethal effects at or below the critical dilution triggers an additional three-monthly retest obligation that changes the applicable monitoring requirements for affected periods in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: If a frequency reduction had been granted, the monitoring frequency for the affected test species reverts to once per quarter until the permit is re-issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A test failure after a granted reduction restores quarterly monitoring; the timing and scope of that reversion change which monitoring intervals were required in FY2025 and whether absent results represent unresolved obligations.

candidates.exact_span: This monitoring frequency reduction applies only until the expiration date of this permit, at which time the monitoring frequency for both test species reverts to once per quarter until the permit is re-issued.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Permit expiration ends any reduced-frequency schedule and restores quarterly testing for both species; whether FY2025 falls before or after expiration changes applicable monitoring frequency and how to interpret missing results near that boundary.

candidates.exact_span: The requirements of this subsection apply only when a toxicity test demonstrates significant lethal effects at or below the critical dilution.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Persistent-toxicity subsection obligations are conditional on a demonstrated significant lethal effect; different readings of that trigger change whether additional persistent-toxicity monitoring requirements were applicable in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Significant toxic effects, are herein defined as a statistically significant difference at the 95% confidence level between the survival of the appropriate test organism in a specified effluent dilution and the control (0% effluent).
candidates.computation_change_reason: This definition governs when a WET result counts as a significant toxic effect, which in turn determines whether persistent-toxicity and retest obligations apply and whether a reported measurement constitutes a limit exceedance versus report-only toxicity monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: If the initial WET test conducted fails, the permittee will conduct three retests.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A failed initial WET test imposes three follow-up retests; whether a given FY2025 test is treated as a failing initial test changes the count and timing of required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: A test that meets all test acceptability criteria and demonstrates significant toxic effects does not need additional confirmation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a valid significant-toxicity result stands without further confirmation affects how many retests are required and whether missing subsequent results should be treated as conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence.

candidates.computation_change_reason: This limits the evidentiary weight of follow-up testing relative to prior results, affecting how missing or conflicting WET data should be classified when establishing compliance state or unresolved missing-evidence cases.
